title: Quantized throughput commitment and notice protocol for Dedicated Capacity
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Purpose: Define an operationally simple but contractually precise approach to committed Dedicated throughput that (a) is measurable, (b) supports autoscaler interaction and burst policies, and (c) maps directly to compensatory credits/remedies. This ticket proposes a 'quantized throughput' model: customers commit to capacity in discrete bands (e.g., 10k TPM, 50k TPM, 200k TPM) instead of continuous tokens/minute curves. The document below defines measurement windows, tolerated degradation bands, error-budget accounting, notification/notice windows, and a formula for crediting. It also specifies how autoscaling events and fleet-level controls (eviction, AZ failover) affect the computation.
proposal_summary: Introduce quantized throughput commitments with a 1-minute aggregation window and 5-minute rolling percentiles. Define three degradation bands (Minor: 95-99% of commitment, Major: 75-95%, Critical: <75%) with proportional credits. Tie notification windows to observed degradation duration and to autoscaler activity: if degradation coincides with an autoscale operation triggered by Redwood, treat differently than customer-directed scaling. Provide contractual language for notice, remediation, and crediting that is explicit and machine-computable.
acceptance_criteria: Define discrete throughput bands and canonical identifiers for use in contracts (e.g., BAND-10K, BAND-50K)
Measurement spec published: aggregation window, percentile rule, and serviceable intervals
Credit formula validated by finance and legal (examples included) and integrated into billing pipeline
Console UI displays banded committed capacity, live measured fulfillment %, and projected error-budget burn
Autoscaler interplay documented and implementation tickets created for runtime and billing teams
measurement_spec: Metric: Committed_Throughput_Fulfillment = Served_Tokens / Committed_Tokens over MeasurementWindow. MeasurementWindow = 5-minute rolling window sampled at 1-minute granularity. Fulfillment percentile = 95th percentile over the calendar month for SLA boundaries. Downtime/maintenance windows excluded per contract notice. If >= 5 consecutive minutes of measurement fall below commitment threshold, count as a degraded interval for credit accrual.
degradation_matrix: Bands and thresholds: Minor degradation (Band fulfillment >=95% and <99%) => Credit = 10% proportional to time in degraded state. Major degradation (>=75% and <95%) => Credit = 30%. Critical degradation (<75%) => Credit = 70%. Credits are computed proportionally to the length of the degraded intervals during the billing month and bucketed per contract: e.g., 10 minutes Major in a month yields prorated credit = 30% * (10min / total_month_minutes) * monthly_commitment_fee.
credit_formula: Monthly_Credit = Sum_over_all_degraded_intervals(DegradationFactor * IntervalMinutes) / TotalBillingMonthMinutes * MonthlyCommitmentFee. DegradationFactor values: Minor=0.10, Major=0.30, Critical=0.70. Example: customer with BAND-50K, monthly fee $50,000 experiences 60 minutes Major and 120 minutes Minor in the month: Credit = (($50k) * ((0.30*60 + 0.10*120) / 44640)) where 44640 = 31 days * 24 * 60. Credits round to nearest dollar and are applied as invoice credit the following billing cycle.
autoscaler_interaction: If degradation coincides with an automatic autoscale operation (triggered by Redwood autoscaler), and the autoscaler successfully restores baseline within the configured autoscale recovery window (default 10 minutes), then Major->Minor crediting may be applied (i.e., use the less severe band) to reflect automatic remediation. If degradation is caused by customer-side configuration (e.g., pinned min capacity set too low) the incident is excluded from crediting. All autoscale actions must be logged and correlated with degraded intervals for adjudication.
notification_escalation_steps: T+0: Automatic alert to customer via email/in-console when 5-minute rolling fulfillment falls below 95% for 5 consecutive minutes
T+15: Pager to technical contacts if degradation persists and falls below 90%
T+60: Formal SLA incident created; primary operations engineer assigned and customer success notified
T+240: Executive escalation and credit calculation kickoff if unresolved after 4 hours
notice_protocol_and_exclusions: Scheduled maintenance windows with >=72 hours customer notice are excluded. Force majeure and customer misconfiguration (network ACLs, VPC routes, on-prem hardware faults) are excluded. If customer requests a deliberate scale-down or change to burst policy, the change takes effect after a 2-hour notice window for SLA accounting. Contracts will include a clause that continuous burst consumption > 2x committed band for >=6 hours will be reclassified and may terminate the enrollment in the committed-band program.
contract_language_snippet: Service Commitment: Redwood will provide Dedicated Capacity at the committed throughput band (identified in Annex A) measured by the 'Committed_Throughput_Fulfillment' metric. If Redwood fails to meet the committed band per the Measurement Spec, customer will receive a pro-rated credit as computed by the Credit Formula. Exclusions: scheduled maintenance, customer misconfiguration, and Force Majeure. Customer must provide an authorized technical contact and enable metrics sharing for adjudication.
billing_and_billing_pipeline_tasks: Engineering must expose per-contract band identifiers to billing, add credit computations into monthly invoice pipeline, and surface provisional credits in the console billing page. Backfill tests: run synthetic degradation scenarios to ensure billing calculations match formula for sample months. Create billing PR: finance/billing#9812.
console_and_observability_requirements: Console needs: (1) committed band display and canonical ID, (2) live fulfillment %, (3) last 24h degradation timeline, (4) projected monthly credit if degradation trends continue. Observability must emit structured events: BAND_COMMITMENT_VIOLATION with fields (band_id, interval_start, interval_end, measured_fulfillment) for easy reconciliation.
rollout_plan: Draft contract language and get Legal sign-off (2 weeks)
Implement measurement instrumentation in runtime (3 sprints)
Add credit computation to billing pipeline and generate test invoices (1 sprint)
Console UI changes for band visibility and alerts (2 sprints)
Pilot with 3 existing Dedicated customers for 6 weeks
Iterate contract verbiage and automation based on pilot feedback, then GA
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Overly generous credits cause margin pressure. Mitigation: cap annual credits at X% of committed revenue (negotiable).
Risk: Ambiguity in root-cause for degradation (Redwood infra vs customer). Mitigation: require metrics sharing and correlate autoscale logs; provide dispute resolution window of 14 days.
Risk: Autoscaler-induced flapping causing spurious credits. Mitigation: introduce recovery hysteresis and only count intervals after stabilization period (default 10 minutes).
notes: Legal prefers example-driven clauses; include 3 worked examples in contract annex.
Finance asked for monthly cap on credits; need to propose typical caps (1%, 3%, 5%) and model impact.
Pilot candidates: AcmeAI (BAND-50K), HealthSync (BAND-10K), Searchly (BAND-200K) — PM outreach pending.
